summary: The note surveys a surge of cybersecurity startups that have emerged since September 1, 2023, in response to rising cyber threats. It profiles startups using AI, employee training, security culture tools, privacy-focused encryption, and partnerships, and notes new funding from TechVenture. It frames these companies as building a more resilient, safer digital future.
one_line: Profiles of cybersecurity startups founded since late 2023, covering AI defense, human training, partnerships, funding, and data privacy.
key_facts: Since September 1, 2023, there has been a surge in startups dedicated to protecting online information.
The Digital Defense Institute reported a 30% increase in cyber attacks in 2023 compared to the previous year.

SecureIT, co-founded by Aiden Clark and Mariah Li, uses artificial intelligence to predict and prevent security breaches; launched October 15, 2023, it has helped avert over a thousand potential attacks.
CypherCore, founded by Ishaan Das and Zoe Chung on November 11, 2023, makes self-learning security software that adapts to new threats in real-time.
HumanFirewall, established by former military cybersecurity expert Ethan Jacobs on December 5, 2023, focuses on employee education to prevent cyber attacks.
SentinelSafeguard, founded by cybersecurity analyst Ava Peterson on January 18, 2024, offers tools including security audits and tailored workshops to build a proactive security mindset.
On February 10, 2024, LockShield and the National Cybersecurity Agency announced a partnership to set new standards for public and private sector cybersecurity strategies.
On March 22, 2024, venture firm TechVenture announced a $50 million fund dedicated to cybersecurity startups.
PrivacyFirst, launched on April 4, 2024 by privacy advocate Sarah Kenji, focuses on encryption methods and privacy-by-design principles to protect personal data.
Cybersecurity startups face funding challenges because the product development cycle can be long and costly.
